rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.Segment`.

**Obligations derived from the text:** The struct has public `kind`, `label` and `ordinal` fields. `Segment::new` builds a segment with no ordinal. `ordinal(self, n)` sets a one-based ordinal. `base(kind, &Label)` formats the kind and label, and `Display` is built on it. `Clone`, `Debug`, `Display`, `PartialEq` and `Eq` are implemented.

**Coverage in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]`:**
- `new`: `Segment::new("fn", Named(["run"]))` is built and `plain.ordinal` is asserted to be `None`.
- `ordinal`: `plain.ordinal(2)` displays as `fn[run]#2` and equals the parsed `segments[1]`, which also has `ordinal == Some(2)`. `segments[2].clone().ordinal(3)` displays as `use@0123456789ab#3`.
- `base` for a named label: `Segment::base("impl", a%2Fb/c%20d)` gives `impl[a%2Fb/c%20d]`. This covers multi-part joining with `/` and percent-encoding of `/` and whitespace. `Segment::base("fn", run)` gives `fn[run]`.
- `base` for a hash label: this has no direct call. It is covered through `Display`, which calls `base`. `segments[2].to_string()` is asserted to be `use@0123456789ab`, so the `kind@hash` branch is checked. The hash label is also asserted to equal `Label::Hash("0123456789ab")`.
- `Display` with and without an ordinal is asserted, for both label variants.
- `Clone`, `PartialEq` and `Debug`: `.clone()` is used, `assert_eq!` compares segments, and `assert_eq!` requires `Debug`. `Eq` is a marker trait that is checked at compile time.
- Field access and `non_exhaustive`: the public fields are read in the test. `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory against rustdoc and checks that the Habeas consumer compiles against the SDK.

**Possible gaps:** I found none. Percent-encoding of the other reserved characters (`%`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@`) belongs to `selector_syntax`, which is a separate requirement. The `Segment` text does not itself ask for it.

text: Describes one step from a selector’s root. `base` formats the kind and label. The optional one-based ordinal disambiguates siblings with the same base.
pub fn new(kind: String, label: Label) -> Self;
pub fn ordinal(self, ordinal: usize) -> Self;
A named label carries decoded name parts. An anonymous label carries the hexadecimal identity hash.
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
